args.question: Hey, I've got 6 legal moves right now: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. There's only 10 empty squares left total. Which of these should I play to end up with the most discs at the end, assuming the opponent plays well? Can you just tell me the best move and why in simple terms?

parts.content:
Best move: **b7**.

Why, simply: it’s the endgame move that gives Black the best final disc count with perfect play. It flips a strong row of White discs on row 7 while keeping the bottom-left empties awkward for White, limiting their clean corner/edge options. The other moves tend to give White better access or more favorable final flips.

args.question: So that last stretch I did all the moves myself without asking you - I figured out a3 then a1 then h1 then g2 would force White to keep passing. Did I actually get lucky there or was that really the best possible line? I want to know if I left points on the table.

parts.content:
That was **not just luck** — if after your move White truly had **no legal moves**, then forcing repeated passes is usually the strongest endgame pattern.

Your final board is **Black 41 – White 23**, so you won by **18 discs**.

The key idea: by playing **a3 → a1 → h1 → g2**, you didn’t just grab discs — you **kept White completely immobile**, so they never got another move to fight back or flip corners/edges. In the endgame, that’s often worth more than any single big flip.

So: **you likely did not leave points on the table in any obvious way**. The pass-chain was the important thing, and you found it.

args.question: Going back earlier - after you told me to play c8 and then a7, White jumped way ahead (like 22 vs 36). Were those actually bad suggestions, or was that just a normal swing that was gonna even out anyway?

parts.content:
From the final board, **Black won 41–23**, so the “22 vs 36” moment was **not automatically a sign the moves were bad**.

In Othello endgames, the score can swing wildly because one move can flip a long line, and if you then force **passes**, you get multiple moves in a row. Your line **a3 → a1 → h1 → g2** looks like it did exactly that: it turned a bad-looking count into a big win by **removing White’s mobility**.

That said: I **can’t prove from this final board alone** whether my earlier **c8** and **a7** were the absolute best moves at those exact positions. To verify that, I’d need the board images from those turns. But the big White lead afterward was very plausibly just a normal temporary swing, not proof those moves were bad.

That actually clears it up a good bit - good to know that big scary lead White had wasn't some disaster I caused, just how the endgame swings go. Glad I double-checked instead of panicking. Final score 41-23, I'm happy calling it done here.
